public.regime_lens: 🚦 RED — both hard deployment gates (TNX, CCC OAS) deteriorated further this week while the geopolitical shock layer sharply re-escalated in parallel, rather than offsetting it · base: Geopolitical Stagflation over Policy Transition, with the fiscal/duration-stress overlay (record US debt, 19-year-high long yields) now compounding a freshly hawkish Fed reaction function under Chair Warsh (explicit inflation-fighting rhetoric, market pricing a coin-flip-plus hike for Sept 16) → WORSENING · shock: two active tracks, now moving in the SAME direction (worsening) rather than diverging as in the prior two updates: (1) Iran/Hormuz — re-escalated hard this week; the US struck Iranian tankers for the first time (Sept 1-2, new "tanker for tanker" policy), and the Strait is reported effectively closed (5-11 vessels/day vs a 13/day 10-day average); Brent spiked ~9% w/w and ~21% m/m to ~$96; (2) a fiscal/duration-stress shock that remains unresolved — 30Y still near its 19-year high above 5.25%, the most recent 30Y auction (mid-August) cleared at the highest yield since 2001 on weak demand, and US federal debt remains above $40T · action: RED = no new deployment; new-tranche silver stays mechanically BLOCKED on both hard rails — TNX 4...
